mainTopic: רב ענן and אליהו, רב יוסף's refusal to pray, the shrinking yeshivos, and Temple workers paid from תרומת הלשכה
overview: The amud finishes the story of רב ענן. רב נחמן thought a man was רב ענן's relative and decided that כבוד תורה comes first. So he judged that man's case before a case about orphans. The other side was too intimidated to argue, and justice was bent. Because of this, אליהו stopped visiting רב ענן. רב ענן fasted and prayed until אליהו came back, but now אליהו frightened him, so רב ענן sat in a box until the teaching was finished. This is why there is a סדר אליהו רבה and a סדר אליהו זוטא. Next, רב יוסף refuses to pray during a time of divine anger. He reasons with a קל וחומר from אלישע, and the גמרא proves from a פסוק that 2,200 students stayed with אלישע. It then lists how many students stayed behind at later yeshivos, a number that kept getting smaller. The גמרא then returns to the list of people paid from תרומת הלשכה, including the inspectors of blemishes, teachers of the כהנים, proofreaders of scrolls and curtain weavers. רב נחמן says the curtain weavers were paid from בדק הבית, and the גמרא defends him from a ברייתא by explaining that it refers to the curtains of the gates. A ברייתא and אבא שאול disagree about who paid the women who raised children for the פרה אדומה. The amud ends as רב הונא begins a question to רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן decides that honoring Torah comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן weighs two positive מצוות and puts the man's case ahead of the orphans' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a positive מצוה and that is a positive מצוה, but the מצוה of honoring Torah wins. So he moved the orphans' case aside and sat down to judge this man's case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן thinks the man is related to רב ענן. He decides that honoring a Torah scholar's family outweighs taking the orphans' case first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judging cases properly is one מצות עשה, and honoring Torah scholars is another. Since both are equal in type, רב נחמן decides that כבוד תורה tips the scale. His decision rests on a mistaken assumption, and that sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment, a מצוה to actively do something
Honor due to the Torah and to those who learn it

phrases.english: This is a positive מצוה and this is a positive מצוה —
phrases.notes: He means: judging cases properly is one מצוה, and honoring Torah scholars and their families is the other.

phrases.english: the positive מצוה of honoring the Torah takes precedence.
He set aside the case of the orphans
and sat down to judge his case,
phrases.notes: "His case" is the case of the man who brought רב ענן the gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב ענן from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two positive מצוות compete, the עשה of כבוד תורה takes precedence.

steps.title: The other side is too intimidated to argue
steps.stepSummary: Seeing the judge honor the man, the opposing side loses the ability to argue his claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the other side saw the honor the judge was showing that man, his arguments were shut down.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows what happened because of רב נחמן's decision. The other side became nervous and could not argue his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one ruled unfairly on purpose. Still, the special treatment frightened the other side into silence, so the trial came out unjust. This is the indirect harm that will be blamed on רב ענן.

keyTerms.meaning: A party in a court case, a litigant
His claims were shut down; he could not argue

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how even a small show of favoritism by a judge can ruin a fair trial.

phrases.english: Once his opposing litigant saw
the honor that he was showing him,
his claims were closed off.
phrases.notes: Literally "his claims got blocked." He was too nervous to argue, so he lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of רב נחמן's decision in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The honor shown to one side silenced the other side, so justice was bent.

steps.title: אליהו stops visiting רב ענן
steps.stepSummary: אליהו used to teach רב ענן regularly, but after this incident he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו used to come to רב ענן regularly, because he was teaching him סדר אליהו. Once רב ענן did this, אליהו went away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us the spiritual result of the bent trial. אליהו, who had been teaching רב ענן, stopped coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן never judged the case himself. Even so, his note and his acceptance of a gift led to an unfair trial, and that was enough for אליהו to leave him.

keyTerms.meaning: Accustomed, used to doing something regularly
The teachings of אליהו that were later collected into a book

phrases.english: With Rav Anan it was customary
that Elijah would come to him,
because he was teaching him
the Order of Elijah.
Once he did this, he departed.
phrases.notes: "This" means causing the unfair trial, through the gift and the note.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב עָנָן הֲוָה רְגִיל אֵלִיָּהוּ דְּאָתֵי גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the consequence of the injustice from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the injustice he caused, רב ענן lost אליהו's visits.

steps.title: רב ענן prays and אליהו returns, but frighteningly
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן fasts and prays. אליהו comes back, but now he scares him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat in a fast and prayed for mercy, and אליהו came. When he came, he would frighten him terribly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן does תשובה through fasting and prayer, and אליהו comes back. The relationship is not fully restored, though, because אליהו now terrifies him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer partly works: אליהו returns. But the fear shows that something has changed between them. This sets up how רב ענן deals with it in the next step.

phrases.english: He sat in a fast
and prayed for mercy, and he came.
When he came,
he would frighten him greatly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ענן responds to אליהו's leaving from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer brought אליהו back, but in a frightening way.

steps.title: רב ענן sits in a box until אליהו finishes teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן protects himself inside a box and keeps learning until אליהו completes the teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made a box and sat in front of him until he finished teaching him his order.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן finds a way to keep learning despite his fear. He sits in a box and stays until אליהו has taught him the whole סדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The box let רב ענן keep learning even though אליהו frightened him. Because of it, the teaching was completed. This sets up the explanation of the two book names in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: And he made a box
and sat before him
until he brought out for him his order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the fear problem from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ענן completed his learning from אליהו by sitting in a box.

steps.title: Why there are two books: סדר אליהו רבה and סדר אליהו זוטא
steps.stepSummary: The story explains the names סדר אליהו רבה and סדר אליהו זוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what people mean when they say: סדר אליהו רבה, the Major Order of Elijah, and סדר אליהו זוטא, the Minor Order of Elijah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the רב ענן story by connecting it to the names of two well-known collections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The larger collection, רבה, was taught before the incident. The smaller one, זוטא, was taught afterward, in the box. So the story explains why the teaching ended up as two works.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what people mean when they say

steps.whatToRemember: Accepting even a small favor led רב ענן to cause an unfair trial, and as a result he lost much of his closeness with אליהו. The two names, רבה and זוטא, preserve that story.

phrases.english: And this is what they say:
The Major Order of Elijah,
and the Minor Order of Elijah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רב ענן story by explaining the two names.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two books, רבה and זוטא, come from before and after רב ענן's mistake.

steps.title: The רבנן ask רב יוסף to pray during divine anger
steps.stepSummary: In רב יוסף's years there was divine anger, and the רבנן ask him to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the years of רב יוסף there was divine anger. The רבנן said to רב יוסף: Let the master pray for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. There is divine anger in רב יוסף's time, and the Sages ask him to pray. This sets up his surprising answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages expect a great leader like רב יוסף to pray and cancel the decree. Their request prepares the way for his refusal in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Divine anger, a harsh decree such as famine
Let the master pray for mercy

phrases.english: In the years of Rav Yosef
there was divine anger.
The Sages said to Rav Yosef:
Let the master pray for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story after the רב ענן story ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Sages ask רב יוסף to pray so the divine anger will be cancelled.

steps.title: רב יוסף refuses, learning from אלישע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues with a קל וחומר: if אלישע did not pray in a time of anger, he should not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Now, אלישע had 2,200 Sages left behind after the Sages took leave of him, and still he did not pray for mercy in a time of divine anger. Should I pray for mercy?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף turns down the request. He compares himself to אלישע, who was far greater and still did not pray in such a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר: אלישע had 2,200 students who stayed with him, and still he did not pray to cancel a famine. So רב יוסף, who sees himself as much smaller, should certainly not pray. He treats a time of divine anger as something even great people did not try to overturn.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if... (opening words of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the 2,200 as everyone who learned with אלישע. They are only the ones who stayed behind after the others left, which shows how big his yeshiva was.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Now, if Elisha,
when the Sages would take leave of him,
there would remain
two thousand two hundred Sages,
at a time of divine anger
would not pray for mercy,
should I pray for mercy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף answers the request from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Using a קל וחומר from אלישע, רב יוסף says he should not pray during divine anger.

steps.title: How do we know 2,200 students stayed with אלישע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the number 2,200 that רב יוסף used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this many stayed behind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask how we know that 2,200 students stayed behind with אלישע. This sets up the proof from a פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's קל וחומר depended on how great אלישע's yeshiva was. The גמרא wants a source in the text for that big number.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this many would remain?
phrases.notes: "This many" means the 2,200 students of אלישע that רב יוסף mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a detail in רב יוסף's argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that 2,200 students stayed behind with אלישע.

steps.title: The פסוק about setting food before a hundred men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where אלישע's servant asks how he can set the food before a hundred men.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And his servant said: How can I set this before a hundred men?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from the story of אלישע feeding people with a small amount of food. The next steps explain how this פסוק gives us the number 2,200.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its face, the פסוק only says 'a hundred men.' The גמרא will need to read it closely to reach 2,200.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And his servant said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֶתֵּן זֶה לִפְנֵי מֵאָה אִישׁ״.
phrases.english: How should I set this before a hundred men?"

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיֹּאמֶר מְשָׁרְתוֹ מָה אֶתֵּן זֶה לִפְנֵי מֵאָה אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source text that answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in מלכים about setting food before a hundred men.

steps.title: What does 'before a hundred men' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand the words 'before a hundred men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'before a hundred men' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the phrase in the פסוק really means. This sets up two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on how these words are read. The גמרא will reject the simple reading and choose another one.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "before a hundred men"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to read the phrase 'before a hundred men.'

steps.title: It cannot mean all the food was for only a hundred men
steps.stepSummary: If all the food was for only one hundred people, that would be a lot of food in a famine, and the servant would have no reason to worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say all of the food was for a hundred men, in famine years that was plenty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading, that all the food together was for a hundred men, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servant sounds worried that the food is not enough. But for only a hundred people, that much food would have been a lot during a famine, so the simple reading does not fit his worry.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a reading about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say that all of it was before a hundred men,
phrases.notes: "All of it" means all the food listed in the פסוק before this one.

phrases.english: in years of famine that was a lot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible reading of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that all the food together was for one hundred men.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That much food would have been plenty for a hundred people in a famine, so the servant's worry would make no sense.

steps.title: Each portion was for a hundred men
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that each separate portion of food had to feed a hundred men, so there were 2,200 people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, each and every portion was before a hundred men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading: every single portion of food was meant for a hundred people. This proves the 2,200 number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the 22 portions had to feed a hundred men, so the total was 2,200. That matches the number of students רב יוסף said stayed with אלישע.
steps.whatToRemember: The 2,200 students of אלישע come from reading the פסוק to mean that each portion of food fed a hundred men.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that each and every one
phrases.notes: Twenty loaves plus two other portions of food, each for a hundred men, comes to 2,200.

phrases.english: was before a hundred men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכֹל חַד וְחַד קַמֵּי מֵאָה אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after rejecting the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each portion fed a hundred men, so 2,200 were there.

steps.title: How many stayed behind at the yeshivos of רב and רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: 1,200 students stayed behind at רב's yeshiva and 800 at רב הונא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the students left רב's yeshiva, 1,200 still remained. At רב הונא's yeshiva, 800 remained.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just counted אלישע's students, it now gives the counts for later yeshivos, starting with רב and רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information added along the way, not a proof. The numbers get smaller from one generation to the next.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: When the students would take leave from the yeshiva of רב,
1,200 students would remain.

phrases.aramaic: מִבֵּי רַב הוּנָא, הֲווֹ פָּיְישִׁי תַּמְנֵי מְאָה רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: From the yeshiva of רב הונא, 800 students would remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from אלישע's count to the counts of later yeshivos.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 1,200 remained at רב's yeshiva and 800 at רב הונא's.

steps.title: The huge crowds at רב הונא's yeshiva
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא needed 13 speakers to pass on his lecture, and the dust from his students' cloaks could block the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא taught through 13 speakers. When his students stood up and shook out their cloaks, the dust rose and hid the sun, and in ארץ ישראל people said, 'They just stood up in the yeshiva of רב הונא the Babylonian.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how huge רב הונא's crowd was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crowd was too big for one voice, so 13 people repeated his words. The dust cloud was so big that people in ארץ ישראל knew what it meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Speakers who repeated the teacher's words aloud to the crowd

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא הֲוָה דָּרֵישׁ בִּתְלֵיסַר אָמוֹרָאֵי.
phrases.english: רב הונא would lecture through thirteen speakers.
phrases.notes: Here אמוראי are people who called out the teacher's words so the whole crowd could hear.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ קָיְימִי רַבָּנַן מִמְּתִיבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: When the students would stand up in the yeshiva of רב הונא
and shake out their cloaks,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה סָלֵיק אַבְקָא וְכָסֵי לֵיהּ לְיוֹמָא,
phrases.english: the dust would rise up and cover the sun,
and they would say in the West:
phrases.notes: "The West" is ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: קָמוּ לֵיהּ מִמְּתִיבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּבְלָאָה.
phrases.english: They have stood up in the yeshiva of רב הונא the Babylonian.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא הֲוָה דָּרֵישׁ בִּתְלֵיסַר אָמוֹרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a description of רב הונא's yeshiva after giving its count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's crowds were huge: he needed 13 speakers, and the dust from the students' cloaks blocked out the sun.

steps.title: 400 'orphans' at the yeshiva of רבה and רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: Only 400 stayed behind at the yeshiva of רבה and רב יוסף, and they called themselves orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the students left the yeshiva of רבה and רב יוסף, 400 remained, and they called themselves 'orphans.'
steps.whatsHappening: The count keeps dropping. In the next generation only 400 remained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students felt how small their group was compared to earlier generations, so they called themselves 'orphans.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: When the students would take leave from the yeshiva of רבה and רב יוסף,
400 students would remain,
and they called themselves "orphans."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of yeshivos with a smaller number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 400 remained at the yeshiva of רבה and רב יוסף, and they called themselves orphans.

steps.title: 200 'orphans of orphans' at the yeshiva of אביי
steps.stepSummary: Only 200 stayed behind at the yeshiva of אביי (some say רב פפא or רב אשי), and they called themselves orphans of orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the students left the yeshiva of אביי (some say רב פפא, some say רב אשי), 200 remained, and they called themselves 'orphans of orphans.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last and smallest count in the list: 200 students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are different versions of whose yeshiva this was. Either way, the drop continues, and the students saw themselves as even more alone than the generation before.
steps.whatToRemember: From אלישע (2,200) to רב (1,200), רב הונא (800), רבה and רב יוסף (400), and אביי (200), the number of students who stayed behind kept getting smaller.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי אַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: When the students would take leave from the yeshiva of אביי,
and some say from the yeshiva of רב פפא,
and some say from the yeshiva of רב אשי,
200 students would remain,
and they called themselves "orphans of orphans."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list with the smallest number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 200 remained at the yeshiva of אביי (or רב פפא, or רב אשי), and they called themselves orphans of orphans.

steps.title: Inspectors of blemishes were paid from Temple funds
steps.stepSummary: The people in ירושלים who checked קרבנות for blemishes were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר רדיפא said in the name of רבי אמי: The inspectors of blemishes in ירושלים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story section is over. The גמרא goes back to its list of people who were paid from Temple funds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking animals for blemishes was a service for the whole public, so these inspectors were paid from the public Temple fund.

keyTerms.meaning: Inspectors of blemishes on animals brought as קרבנות
The Temple fund collected from the half-shekels

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רְדִיפָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: רבי יצחק בר רדיפא said that רבי אמי said:
Inspectors of blemishes in Jerusalem
would take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רְדִיפָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the topic of people paid from Temple funds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inspectors of blemishes in ירושלים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Teachers of שחיטה to כהנים were paid from Temple funds
steps.stepSummary: Scholars who taught the laws of שחיטה to the כהנים were also paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Scholars who taught the laws of שחיטה to the כהנים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more kind of worker to the list of people paid from Temple funds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the inspectors, these teachers served the needs of the Temple, so they were also paid from the public fund.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְלַמְּדִין הִלְכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה לְכֹהֲנִים,
phrases.english: Torah scholars who teach the laws of slaughter to the priests
would take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another worker to the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars who taught the laws of שחיטה to the כהנים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Teachers of the laws of the handful are paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: תלמידי חכמים who teach the כהנים the laws of קמיצה are paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: Torah scholars who teach the כהנים the laws of קמיצה take their pay from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more group to its list of Temple workers who were paid from the public Temple fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the teachers of שחיטה in step 19, these scholars are paid by the Temple. The כהנים need to know how to do קמיצה properly so the קרבנות are done right, so teaching it counts as a Temple need.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן scooping a handful of flour from a מנחה (flour offering)

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
Torah scholars who teach
the laws of taking the handful to the priests
take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another group of paid Temple teachers, parallel to the שחיטה teachers in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teachers of the laws of קמיצה to the כהנים are paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Proofreaders of scrolls in ירושלים are paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: the proofreaders of scrolls in ירושלים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the people in ירושלים who checked and corrected scrolls were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another group is added to the list: the people who checked ספרי תורה for mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making sure the scrolls are correct is a service to the whole public, so it is paid for with public Temple money, just like the earlier jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: Proofreaders who check and correct scrolls

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The proofreaders of scrolls in Jerusalem
would take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of workers paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scroll proofreaders in ירושלים were paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Women who weave the curtains are paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: the women who weave the פרוכות were paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: women who weave the curtains of the בית המקדש take their pay from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reports רב's opinion about the curtain weavers. This sets up his own disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far every worker on the list has been paid from תרומת הלשכה. Here רב puts the curtain weavers in the same group. Next, רב נחמן will question whether that is right.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtains of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said:
The women who weave the curtains
take their wages from the collection of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the curtain weavers to the list, and opens the way for רב נחמן's own view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, curtain weavers are paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: רב נחמן says the curtain weavers are paid from the building fund
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives his own view: the weavers are paid from קדשי בדק הבית, because the curtains take the place of walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I say they are paid from the money set aside for fixing and keeping up the בית המקדש, since the curtains are made in place of the building itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees with what he just quoted. He says the weavers' pay comes from a different Temple fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate Temple funds. תרומת הלשכה pays for the daily needs and קרבנות, while בדק הבית pays for the building. Since a curtain works like a wall, רב נחמן says weaving it is building work and belongs to the building fund.

keyTerms.meaning: Money dedicated for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש building
But I say (the speaker's own opinion)
In place of the building or wall

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two funds. תרומת הלשכה is the yearly half-shekel money for קרבנות and daily needs. בדק הבית is a separate fund just for the building.

phrases.english: But I say: from the funds consecrated for Temple maintenance.
phrases.notes: The "I" here is רב נחמן himself, giving his own opinion after quoting רב.

phrases.english: Since the curtains are made in place of the building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן offers his own opinion against the one he quoted from רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Curtain weavers are paid from בדק הבית, because curtains act as part of the building.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the curtain weavers were paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא that lists curtain weavers, the house of גרמו and the house of אבטינס, all paid from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: the women who weave the curtains, the house of גרמו who made the לחם הפנים, and the house of אבטינס who made the קטורת were all paid from תרומת הלשכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's view using an older teaching that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly puts the curtain weavers with groups paid from תרומת הלשכה. That seems to go straight against רב נחמן, who said they were paid from בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The family in charge of baking the לחם הפנים
The family in charge of making the קטורת
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
The incense burned in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The women who weave the curtains,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית גַּרְמוּ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: and the house of Garmu, in charge of making the showbread,
and the house of Avtinas, in charge of making the incense,

phrases.aramaic: — כּוּלָּן הָיוּ נוֹטְלוֹת שְׂכָרָן מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה!
phrases.english: all of them would take their wages from the collection of the chamber!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's opinion from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that curtain weavers are paid from בדק הבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says curtain weavers were paid from תרומת הלשכה, which goes against רב נחמן.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the curtains of the gates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about gate curtains, which are not in place of the building.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the ברייתא is talking about the curtains of the gates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן by saying the ברייתא and רב נחמן are talking about different curtains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gate curtains hang in doorways and do not replace any wall, so they are not building work and are paid from תרומת הלשכה. רב נחמן was talking about curtains that do replace a wall, so those are paid from בדק הבית.

phrases.english: There, it is referring to the curtains of the gates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different kinds of curtains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to cover every curtain, including the ones that replace walls.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means gate curtains. Curtains that replace walls are paid from בדק הבית, as רב נחמן said.

steps.title: רב's list of thirteen curtains in the מקדש שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רב that there were thirteen curtains in the second בית המקדש, including seven at the gates, which shows that gate curtains existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said in the name of רב: there were thirteen curtains in the second בית המקדש. Seven were by the seven gates, one was at the entrance of the היכל, one at the entrance of the אולם, two were in the דביר, and two matched them above in the upper floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing there really were curtains at the gates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list splits the curtains into types. The seven gate curtains are the ones the ברייתא meant. The two in the דביר, which took the place of a wall, are the kind רב נחמן meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The main hall of the Sanctuary
The entrance hall in front of the היכל
The inner area, the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that curtains that replace walls are building work, paid from בדק הבית. The ברייתא's curtain weavers, paid from תרומת הלשכה, are explained as weavers of the gate curtains, which are only doorway hangings.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה פָּרֹכוֹת הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: There were thirteen curtains in the Second Temple:
seven opposite the seven gates,
one at the entrance of the Sanctuary,
and one at the entrance of the Entrance Hall.
Two in the inner sanctum,
and two corresponding to them in the upper chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 25 by showing that gate curtains existed.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא refers to gate curtains
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's list, quoted by רבי זירא, of the thirteen curtains in the second בית המקדש, seven of them at the gates

steps.title: Women raising children for the פרה אדומה were paid from the Temple fund
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the women who raised their children for the פרה אדומה took their wages from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The women who raised their children for the פרה אדומה took their wages from תרומת הלשכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds another group to its list of people paid from תרומת הלשכה: the women who raised children for the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed curtain weavers, the house of גרמו and the house of אבטינס. This ברייתא adds one more Temple-related job paid from the public fund. Raising these children was a service to the whole community, so it is paid from the community's Temple money.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the פרה אדומה (red heifer), whose ashes purify from טומאת מת
The fund collected from the yearly half-shekel donations and kept in the Temple chamber

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Women who raise their children for the red heifer
would take their wages
from the collection of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the list of Temple workers paid from תרומת הלשכה, continuing the theme of steps 22-26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women who raised children for the פרה אדומה were paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: אבא שאול says wealthy women of ירושלים supported them
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול disagrees: the wealthy, prominent women of ירושלים fed and supported these mothers, so the Temple fund did not pay them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: The prominent women of ירושלים would feed them and support them.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול argues with the first opinion in the ברייתא and says the money came from private donors, not the Temple fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that public Temple money paid these women. אבא שאול says the wealthy women of ירושלים took this on themselves, so there was no need for תרומת הלשכה. The disagreement is only about who paid, not about whether the women were supported.

keyTerms.meaning: Feed and provide a living for

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: the first opinion says תרומת הלשכה paid the women who raised children for the פרה; אבא שאול says the wealthy women of ירושלים supported them.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
The prominent women of Jerusalem
would feed them and provide them with a livelihood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the same ברייתא about the source of payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wealthy women of ירושלים supported the mothers, so they were not paid from תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: רב הונא begins to ask רב a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a question that רב הונא asked רב; the question itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא asked רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move: רב הונא is about to ask רב a question, which appears right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בעא מיניה introduces a real question where the asker does not know the answer. The content of the question and its answer follow in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him: introduces a question to a teacher

phrases.english: Rav Huna asked of Rav:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transition line opening a new question after the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of the question comes in the next part of the גמרא.
